# Subway Seat for CSS variables

Every role as a custom property, with an -rgb triplet beside it for transparency, and the diff tints as --ss-diff-* (line and word grounds for added, removed and changed text). subway-seat-flavors.css holds all three, switched by data-theme or the system light/dark setting.

[CSS variables](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Cascading_variables/Using_custom_properties) · [Previews and copy buttons](https://oddurs.github.io/subway-seat/ports/css/)

## Turn it on

**Subway Seat**, in your stylesheet:

```css
@import url("subway-seat.css");

body {
  background: var(--ss-base);
  color: var(--ss-text);
}

.scrim {
  background: rgb(var(--ss-crust-rgb) / 0.8);
}
```

**Subway Seat Tunnel**, in your stylesheet:

## Follow light and dark

In your stylesheet:

```css
@import url("subway-seat-flavors.css");

/* Enamel when the system is light, Walnut when it's dark;
   data-theme="walnut" | "tunnel" | "enamel" on <html> picks one instead. */
```

## Uninstall

- Delete `styles/subway-seat.css`.
- Delete `styles/subway-seat-tunnel.css`.
- Delete `styles/subway-seat-enamel.css`.
- Delete `styles/london-moquette.css`.
- Delete `styles/london-deep-level.css`.
- Delete `styles/london-portland.css`.
- Delete `styles/subway-seat-flavors.css`.
- Remove the line you added to turn it on.
